subject.title: fix(opencode): public models work without configured credentials

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally support OpenCode Zen’s credentialless `public`-key mode for catalog models whose input pricing is zero, even though the current OpenClaw and OpenCode user documentation still require a configured API key?
rationale: Tests and live proof establish that the patch can implement the behavior, but they cannot decide whether an undocumented upstream client behavior should become a supported OpenClaw provider contract and plugin API commitment.

options.title: Adopt the public-model contract
options.body: Approve the credentialless mode as a supported OpenCode integration, then merge with provider documentation updated to define the model-eligibility and fallback boundary.

options.title: Hold the current credential requirement
options.body: Keep OpenCode Zen credential-gated until the upstream provider publishes or confirms a stable anonymous-inference contract that OpenClaw can support.

options.title: Request a narrower explicit integration contract
options.body: Ask for provider-owner confirmation and a documented eligibility source before accepting any model-scoped synthetic-auth extension.

recommendation.title: Hold the current credential requirement
recommendation.body: Keep OpenCode Zen credential-gated until the upstream provider publishes or confirms a stable anonymous-inference contract that OpenClaw can support.

likelyOwner.reason: They assembled the provider-contract evidence and can route the proposed contract to the appropriate OpenCode integration owner, though final direction remains a repository decision.
